layer1_summary.paragraph: The front matter of Iron Arrow: A History establishes the book's origins, its authors' credentials, and the profound significance of preserving the society's legacy before key records and memories were lost forever. Written by Randolph H. Femmer, a 1968 Iron Arrow member and University of Miami alumnus, and illustrated by Thaddius J. Koch, Jr., the work represents a labor of love that transformed scattered fragments of institutional memory into a unified historical record.
bullets: Randolph H. Femmer, an Iron Arrow member since 1968 who served as both Homecoming Chairman and a "Medicine Man" of the society, authored the history as a deeply personal act of preservation rooted in his own membership experience.

Thaddius J. Koch, Jr., who served as Chairman of the 1969 Carni Gras and was himself elected to Iron Arrow, provided the illustrations, making the book a collaborative effort between two committed alumni.

Thurston Adams, Director of Student Activities Emeritus at the University of Miami, offered a testimonial warning that without this history, the preponderance of Iron Arrow's accumulated facts and happenings would have been lost forever within just a few more years.

Francis Houghtaling, identified as the first member of Iron Arrow, gave an emotionally charged endorsement, describing the history as so vivid and stirring that it sent chills running up and down his spine.

The invocation poem encapsulates Iron Arrow's foundational ethic — that true membership requires openly demonstrated love of Alma Mater, given without thought of personal reward — setting the moral tone for everything that follows.

layer2_details.text:
INVOCATION
- The invocation text reads: "He who would know the ARROW / must as an irrefutable rule / have openly and without / thought of reward / shown obvious love / of Alma Mater"
- No author attribution is given for the invocation verse
- The invocation appears on the front matter page alongside endorsement quotes

INTRODUCTION
- Full title of the work: *Iron Arrow: A History, Seventy-Five Years*
- Author: Randolph H. Femmer
- Illustrator: Thadius J. Koch, Jr.
- Copyright: © 1976, Iron Arrow Honor Society, University of Miami
- First Printing: 1976, University Press
- Second Printing: 1989, University Press
- Third Printing: 2001, Friesens Corp.
- Randolph H. Femmer became a member of Iron Arrow in 1968
- Femmer served as Chairman of Homecoming at the University of Miami in 1968
- Femmer held the role of "Medicine Man" of Iron Arrow
- After graduation, Femmer ran for the U.S. Congress in Missouri
- Femmer authored *The Mushroom Mutiny – An Alternative To War*; this was his second book; he is identified as a biologist
- Thadius J. Koch, Jr. received his master's degree in art at the University of Miami in 1973
- As an undergraduate, Koch served as Chairman of the 1969 Carni Gras and was elected to membership in Iron Arrow
- Koch is described as a naturalist with activities including canoeing, camping, orchid-cultivating, and photography
- Endorsement from Thurston Adams, Director of Student Activities, Emeritus, University of Miami: "You have done a tremendous amount of research; collecting so many, many facts and happenings, assembled them, recorded them; and, put them together so beautifully. No one of us ever had more than a fragment of knowledge of the entirety of the things you give to us in this history! In a few more years, the preponderance of of these data would have been lost forever. Blessings always!"
- Endorsement from Francis Houghtaling, identified as "First member of Iron Arrow": "Randolph H. Femmer has created a word picture of the founding of the real University of Miami through the History of Iron Arrow. His description colors the real life of a University because it tells of the students who made it possible to be the greatest University of this century founded by private funds."
- Second quote attributed to Francis Houghtaling: "If I don't stop reading this history, I'm going to catch pneumonia from the chills running up and down my spine."
- Photograph of Native American scene reprinted by permission of the Miami Public Library
